conditions.text: Set up app version 3.3.0 on iOS 18.4, device model iPhone15,2 — these were identical across all analyzed events.
Push should be in a deliverable state: OS permission ALLOWED and provider registration REGISTERED, as reported for every event.
The user profile was consistent in all events, so reproduce with a normal, consistent profile.
The news_v2 flag is not a required condition: it was on in 2 events and off in 1, so the crash occurred in both states.
No suspect commit was identified, so there is no specific code change to check out or revert as part of the setup.

missing_evidence_questions.text: What was in the GET /api/news 200 response body (item count, paging cursors, total pages) that could make loadPage compute an index of -1? The packet records only the status code.
What page or offset state existed before the load-more tap — e.g. had the user already paged to the end, or scrolled back? The packet lists only foreground, navigate, tap and the backend call.
Why did no suspect commit surface for feed.ts:88 — is the file outside the analyzed history, or unchanged recently?
Do the 3 events differ in anything besides the news_v2 flag (for example locale, network conditions, or account data) that the packet did not capture?
Does the crash reproduce on other app versions, OS versions or devices, given all analyzed events share 3.3.0 / iOS 18.4 / iPhone15,2?

steps_prose.text: Bring the app to the foreground (this lifecycle step was present in all 3 events).
Let the feed request complete: GET /api/news returns 200, so the backend call succeeds rather than failing.
At that point loadPage (src/modules/news/feed.ts line 88) raises RangeError: Invalid page index -1.

summary.text: Across 3 analyzed events, a RangeError "Invalid page index -1" is thrown in loadPage at src/modules/news/feed.ts:88 after the news feed loads more items following a tap on the load-more button.
